title: Restoration of the Elders
english: …Then also, you have arranged us, the elders, who were already exhausted by time, by the weakness of the body, and by the multitude of tribulations (for the many now moved about us weighed down our life), and you, who are living in spirit, are cooling us, bringing us back from the state of animal lairs into a moderate and life-giving wakefulness.
Therefore the statement is such, and it is possible to think of it simply, and to receive a word that is unshakable.
The simpler one, which is able to be presented to everyone from what is at hand, is this: that Cain must be given sevenfold the recompense for what he sinned (Genesis 4:15).

For it is not the part of a righteous judge to mark out equal returns; rather, it is necessary to pay the debts to the one who has begun to do evil with an addition, or perhaps he himself will become better through the punishments, and make the rest more self-controlled by the example.
translator_notes: The Greek text is a fragment cut mid-sentence at the beginning and end.
The phrase 'νεναρκηκότας' is a perfect middle participle, indicating a state resulting from a completed action.
The phrase 'φωλεύοντα τῶν ζώων' is translated as 'animal lairs' to maintain the metaphor of the believers' state before being awakened.
The phrase 'ἐκ τοῦ προχείρου' is translated as 'from what is at hand' to reflect the ease of presentation.

title: The Significance of Seven
english: …Having multiplied sevenfold, he set the limit within it. And for seven years the Hebrew was released from slavery. In the past, they made the named Jubilee consisting of seven weeks of years, in which the land rested (Leviticus 25:4), debts were cut off, and there was a release from slavery; and a new life was established from the beginning in the seventh number, in a certain way receiving the completion of the old.

These things are types of this present age, which runs us through by means of the seven days; in which the forgiveness of more moderate sins takes place, according to the philanthropic care of the good Master, so that we are not handed over to punishment for an endless age. The sevenfold, then, is because of the relationship to this world, as if of the beauty-loving men from them…
translator_notes: The Greek text is fragmentary, beginning and ending mid-sentence; the translation reflects this with ellipses.
The opening clause 'ἑπτὰ πολυπλασιάσας' refers to the act of multiplying sevenfold.
